-| `hashtext('byosmtp.campaign_start:' \|\| user_id)` | `internal/platformapi` `createJob` (Phase 4 §8, P4-7) | transaction-scoped (`pg_advisory_xact_lock`); auto-released on commit/rollback | Per-user lock serializing the one-active-campaign-per-user check-then-insert; a DYNAMIC key (hash of `byosmtp.campaign_start:<user_id>`), not a fixed reserved value, so it is exempt from the fixed-key registry above by construction (the spec's own §8 pseudocode). `hashtext` returns a 32-bit hash spread across the full `int4` range (positive and negative), so it is not confined to the reserved `8_000_000_000–8_999_999_999` band, but the collision surface is a different user's SAME lock call, not the migration runner or the Brain singleton (whose keys are fixed literals far outside `hashtext`'s typical output) — practically negligible, and the lock's blast radius on a false collision is a serialized (not incorrect) check, never data corruption. |

-| POST | `/v1/quote` | Phase 3; M3-Phase 7 | **M3-Phase 7 §4 (M3-P7-OD-11): a FEASIBILITY check, not a cost lookup** — module 3 prices as a flat monthly subscription (`module-3-build-plan.md` §1: no per-send charge, no per-recipient price), so `quote` answers *"can this run, how many recipients, within which cap, and roughly how long at current capacity?"* rather than computing a bill. Body now requires `user_id` (M3-P7-OD-5 — every field below is per-user; additive to the request) alongside `recipient_count`. Response: `feasible` (bool — **`false` means the request CANNOT be accepted as submitted**; a campaign merely exceeding today's daily capacity is `true` with a long projection, never `false` — conflating "slow" with "cannot run" is the one thing this endpoint must never do), `reasons[]` (empty when feasible; one entry per binding constraint — `exceeds_queue_cap` carrying `limit`/`requested`/`cap_name`, `no_eligible_accounts`, `all_accounts_unverified`, `from_gate_blocked`, `dispatch_disabled`), `capacity` (`eligible_accounts`, `daily_capacity_remaining`, `effective_concurrency`, and — **REQUIRED and non-null on every `feasible:true` response, never omitted** — `estimated_duration_sec` + `estimate_basis:"current_eligible_capacity"`, both entirely omitted together only when `quote_capacity_projection_enabled=false`), `caps` (the user's resolved `queue_depth_cap`/`daily_send_cap`/`account_count_cap`, override→global per M3-Phase 6 §1), and `warnings[]` (empty by default; an explicit `long_duration` object — `code`, `estimated_duration_sec`, `threshold_sec` — appears when the projection crosses `quote_long_duration_warn_sec`, never a bare number the caller must independently judge). The legacy `cost`/`currency`/`unit_price_credits`/`tier` fields are **retained** (Rule 5 — never removed) but are now **inert**: `unit_price_credits` is seeded `0` (`byosmtp_0048`), so `cost` is always `0` at the default — the fields exist purely for contract compatibility with the additive shape module 2 established, not meaningful pricing. Pure, side-effect-free, idempotent — reserves nothing and creates no job. **`recipient_count` rejections are distinguishable** (see the `details[]` note above): absent/`null` → `required`; present-but-negative → `out_of_range`; wrong JSON type → `malformed` naming the field. `0` is a VALID count, not a rejection |
-| POST | `/v1/run` | Phase 3; M3-Phase 4/5 | accept a job — body `{job_item_id, user_id}` (both UUIDs; `user_id` = owning tenant, REQUIRED) → create one `byosmtp.jobs` row, return `202` immediately (async kickoff; never blocks on the send). The `job_item_id` must belong to `user_id` (else `404 not_found`). Duplicate `job_item_id` for the same tenant → clean `200` with the existing job (idempotent; never a raw `23505`). **One active campaign per user (M3-Phase 4 §8, P4-7):** if `user_id` already has a DIFFERENT campaign active (any non-terminal job), the run is rejected outright with `409 conflict` (internal reason `user_campaign_active`) and creates ZERO job rows — enforced under a per-user Postgres advisory lock so concurrent attempts are genuinely serialized, not racy. **Module 3 M3-Phase 5 §5.2/§6.4, same advisory-locked transaction:** a SUSPENDED user's enqueue is refused outright (`409 conflict`, `user_suspended`) — accepting work into a queue that cannot drain is not losslessness. Exceeding `max_campaign_size` (this campaign's own job count) → `409 conflict` (`max_campaign_size_reached`); exceeding `max_queued_jobs` (the user's TOTAL live queue across all campaigns) → `409 conflict` (`max_queued_jobs_reached`) — both resolved per-user override→global (`byosmtp.user_config_overrides`, admin-writable). On the FIRST job of a campaign, `/v1/run` also upserts a `byosmtp.campaigns` row, resolving and FREEZING `campaign_expiry_sec` into `expires_at` (a later config/override change never retroactively moves an already-started campaign's expiry) |
-| GET | `/v1/report` | Phase 3; M3-Phase 5/6/7 | reflect a job's state — `?user_id=<uuid>` (REQUIRED tenant selector) plus `?job_id=` or `?job_item_id=`: returns `state`, `provider_message_id` (when `sent`), `completed_at`, `attempt_count` — clean external state only. **`provider_message_id`/`completed_at` are OMITTED (key absent, not `null`) until set** — a UI must check for key presence, not for `null`, on this single-job shape. A job owned by another tenant → `404 not_found` (no existence disclosure). **M3-Phase 7 (§1.1, M3-P7-OD-1) widens this shape with three more OMITTED-until-set fields: `smtp_response` (the box's own scrubbed provider text — never the internal reason, never a credential), `error_class` (the locked `byosmtp.error_class` enum's text value), `failed_at` (an alias of `completed_at`, present only when the state is a genuine terminal `failed`/`bounced`).** All three are present whenever the job has a recorded failure detail (including a job currently `queued`/`assigned`/`sending` after a failed attempt that requeued — the sticky "why did the last attempt fail" fact), and are ALL OMITTED once the job reaches `sent` — the underlying columns are sticky-by-design and would otherwise show a stale failure reason on a job that ultimately succeeded. NEVER reads `last_error_message` (the internal-slug-carrying column) — enforced by the `user_output_scrub` CI gate, not merely by convention. **M3-Phase 7 (§2) also adds `account_id`/`account_username` — the per-account attribution delta**: which of the user's OWN accounts sent (or is assigned to send) this job, read from `jobs.assigned_account_id` via a `LEFT JOIN byosmtp.accounts`. Both are OMITTED (key absent, not `null`) until the job is dispatched — a `queued` job never assigned, or one requeued and cleared, has neither key, matching this shape's existing omit-the-key convention. `account_username` is the human-readable `smtp_username` — the actual product feature (a uuid alone answers nothing for a user). The accounts join is NEVER what enforces tenancy (`jobs.user_id = $user_id` alone does); a cross-tenant probe gets the same `404 not_found` as ever, with no account field leaked. **M3-Phase 5 (§5.4):** a job WAITING for capacity — its only accounts self-recovering (throttle/daily-limit paused), or its user having zero accounts — reads as clean pending `state:"queued"` (never `failed`, never an error, even if it waits until the next daily reset); a job whose entire eligible account set is truly exhausted (all accounts quarantined/disabled/manual-paused) reads `state:"failed"`. The internal reason (`accounts_exhausted`, which accounts, why — renamed from `pool_exhausted` at G3, M3-P2-OD-3) is NEVER surfaced — two-vocabulary rule. **M3-Phase 6 (§2):** a job RECLAIMED from a dead/hung box (heartbeat-miss or lease-expiry) returns to clean pending `state:"queued"` with an incremented `attempt_count` (saturating) — the internal reclaim reason (`box heartbeat missed`/`lease expired`, `actor='reclaim_loop'`) stays internal and is never surfaced; a persistently-reclaimed job never fails by attempt count (it fails only on true account exhaustion, §2.5). **B8 (Phase 9 contract completion) — `?campaign_id=<uuid>` mode:** when `campaign_id` is present (instead of `job_id`/`job_item_id`), `report` returns the CAMPAIGN-scoped aggregate shape below rather than the single-job shape. |
+| POST | `/v1/quote` | Phase 3; M3-Phase 7 | **M3-Phase 7 §4 (M3-P7-OD-11): a FEASIBILITY check, not a cost lookup** — module 3 prices as a flat monthly subscription (`module-3-build-plan.md` §1: no per-send charge, no per-recipient price), so `quote` answers *"can this run, how many recipients, within which cap, and roughly how long at current capacity?"* rather than computing a bill. Body now requires `user_id` (M3-P7-OD-5 — every field below is per-user; additive to the request) alongside `recipient_count`. Response: `feasible` (bool — **`false` means the request CANNOT be accepted as submitted**; a campaign merely exceeding today's daily capacity is `true` with a long projection, never `false` — conflating "slow" with "cannot run" is the one thing this endpoint must never do), `reasons[]` (empty when feasible; one entry per binding constraint — `exceeds_queue_cap` carrying `limit`/`requested`/`cap_name`, `no_eligible_accounts`, `all_accounts_unverified`, `from_gate_blocked`, `dispatch_disabled`), `capacity` (`eligible_accounts`, `daily_capacity_remaining`, `effective_concurrency`, and — **REQUIRED and non-null on every `feasible:true` response, never omitted** — `estimated_duration_sec` + `estimate_basis:"current_eligible_capacity"`, both entirely omitted together only when `quote_capacity_projection_enabled=false`), `caps` (the user's resolved `queue_depth_cap`/`daily_send_cap`/`account_count_cap`, override→global per M3-Phase 6 §1), and `warnings[]` (empty by default; an explicit `long_duration` object — `code`, `estimated_duration_sec`, `threshold_sec` — appears when the projection crosses `quote_long_duration_warn_sec`, never a bare number the caller must independently judge). Pure, side-effect-free, idempotent — reserves nothing and creates no job. **`recipient_count` rejections are distinguishable** (see the `details[]` note above): absent/`null` → `required`; present-but-negative → `out_of_range`; wrong JSON type → `malformed` naming the field. `0` is a VALID count, not a rejection |
+| POST | `/v1/run` | Phase 3; M3-Phase 4/5 | accept a job — body `{job_item_id, user_id}` (both UUIDs; `user_id` = owning tenant, REQUIRED) → create one `send_byo.jobs` row, return `202` immediately (async kickoff; never blocks on the send). Exceeding `account_count_cap_per_user` (non-deleted accounts, global-only dial) → `409 conflict` (`account_cap_reached`). **Verify-on-add is MANDATORY** (connect + STARTTLS + AUTH only, no test send): the create always returns `201` with the account object regardless of the verification outcome — a failed verification does NOT roll back the row (the credential is already encrypted and stored; the user can fix it with one PATCH). The `verification` block: `{state: "unverified"\|"verified"\|"failed", verified_at?, verify_at?, code?, smtp_response?}` — `code`/`smtp_response` present only on `"failed"`. `smtp_response` is a deliberate widening of the response envelope for this surface only (M3-P3-OD-3) — the scrubbed provider text, never the internal reason. |
+| GET | `/v1/send-byo/accounts` | M3-Phase 3 | list the caller's OWN accounts — `?user_id=<uuid>` is MANDATORY and SERVER-ENFORCED (never an optional filter, unlike the admin list). Cursor-paginated on `(created_at, id)`, same keyset shape as the admin list |
+| GET | `/v1/send-byo/accounts/{id}` | M3-Phase 3 | read one account, scoped to `?user_id=<uuid>`. Never includes the secret/ciphertext/nonce/key id — `has_credential` is the only credential-related field |
+| PATCH | `/v1/send-byo/accounts/{id}` | M3-Phase 3 | update, scoped to `?user_id=<uuid>`. Omit = unchanged (structural for `smtp_secret`: the credential columns are absent from the SET list entirely when the field is omitted). `user_id` is NOT a patchable field — it does not exist in the request schema, so an attempt to send it is rejected by the strict decoder before any handler logic runs |
+| GET | `/v1/send-byo/accounts/{id}/events` | M3-Phase 3 | the account's own audit trail, scoped to `user_id` (not `account_id` alone — a purged account's events row has `account_id` nulled, so scoping by `user_id` keeps it reachable and keeps a cross-tenant probe against a foreign account id from returning anything) |
+| POST | `/v1/send-byo/accounts/{id}/disable`, `/v1/send-byo/accounts/{id}/enable`, `/v1/send-byo/accounts/{id}/pause`, `/v1/send-byo/accounts/{id}/unpause` | M3-Phase 3 | re-scoped lifecycle transitions (module 2's engine, unchanged logic). `unpause` refuses to clear a non-`manual` pause (`pause_reason` is not `'manual'`) — the one piece of user-safety logic that makes exposing it to users safe at all. `quarantine` is **NOT exposed here** — it stays operator-only (`manual` quarantine, via `/v1/admin/accounts/{id}/quarantine`) |
+| POST | `/v1/send-byo/accounts/{id}/unquarantine` | M3-Phase 5 | **§2**: self-serve un-quarantine, rate-limited (`unquarantine_max_per_day` per ACCOUNT per day; beyond it, refused `422 unprocessable` `unquarantine_rate_limited` and the quarantine sticks until operator action) unless a **test-verified bypass** applies (§2.4: a `credential_verification_state='verified'` result whose `credential_verified_at` postdates `quarantined_at` AND is within `unquarantine_evidence_ttl_sec` — pass the account's test button first, then this route). Refused `422 unprocessable` `not_in_state:quarantined` if the account is not currently quarantined. A refusal writes NO audit row; a success writes one `account_events` row (`action='unquarantine'`, `actor='user'`) recording which reason was cleared and whether the bypass was used. A success ALSO stamps `cleared_at` on the account's live `account_quarantined` notification row, in the SAME transaction (2026-08-03, defect #134 — see the alert-webhook section's "until it clears" note for why the absence of this silently withheld the NEXT quarantine's notification for a day). No request body fields. Returns `200` with the account object |
+| POST | `/v1/send-byo/accounts/{id}/test` | M3-Phase 3/4 | connect + STARTTLS + AUTH only (the SAME `push_verify` path as create's verify-on-add — not a copy) **AND, since M3-Phase 4 §2.5, re-runs the From-alignment check** against the account's CURRENT `from_address`/`smtp_host`/`smtp_username` (no request field changes them — the button re-checks what is already stored, it never changes it). Body accepts one optional field: `{"acknowledge_alignment_warning": true}`. **Available WHILE quarantined** (§3.4: the predicate is `user_id` + not-deleted only, deliberately not gated on quarantined/disabled/paused, since a user cannot produce the un-quarantine evidence if the evidence-producing endpoint is itself gated on not being quarantined). Rate-limited PER ACCOUNT (`account_test_rate_limit_per_day`) — refused with `429 rate_limited` beyond it, counting every attempt (success or failure alike, M3-P3-OD-15). **The From-gate re-check is NOT subject to this rate limit** (§2.4's own precedent — DNS lookups carry no worker-IP-reputation risk). Returns `200` with `{"verification": {"state", "smtp_response"?, "code"?}, "from_alignment": {"state", "dmarc_policy"?, "checked_at"?, "message"?, ...}}` — a FAILED credential test OR a WARN/BLOCK From verdict is still a successful API call (the caller asked "what's the current state" and got a real answer). **M3-P4-OD-17: a fresh unacknowledged WARN verdict is ALWAYS persisted** (never refuses the call, unlike create/PATCH — the test button has no other fields to refuse, and refusing would silently no-op on the request whose entire purpose is reporting the current state); the account simply stays non-routable until a later Test/PATCH supplies the acknowledgment. **M3-P4-OD-18: an unavailable/erroring credential check never hides an already-computed `from_alignment` result** — `verification.state` becomes `"unavailable"` rather than the whole request failing. An indeterminate From-gate check (DNS ignorance) leaves the stored verdict untouched and reports `from_alignment.state: "indeterminate"` instead of a stale or fabricated result |
+| POST | `/v1/send-byo/accounts/{id}/test-send` | M3-Phase 3 | a REAL send (full `push_job`, MAIL FROM/RCPT TO/DATA) to the account's OWN `from_address` only (M3-P3-OD-5: an arbitrary recipient would make this a one-message open relay). FORCES the clicked account specifically (M3-P3-OD-16) — never the cross-account selection a campaign send uses; an ineligible clicked account fails outright (`409 conflict`, `account_not_eligible_for_test_send`) rather than silently substituting a different one. `409 conflict` (`no_worker_available`) if no worker is connected. Writes a real `job`/`job_events` row (Rule 5: an unreported real send is as dishonest as a fabricated one) and consumes a `daily_sent_count` unit. Returns `202` with `{job_id, state:"sending"}` — poll `/v1/report?job_id=...` for the outcome, exactly like any other async send |
+| POST | `/v1/send-byo/accounts/bulk` | M3-Phase 3 | create N accounts in one request — body `{user_id, accounts: [{smtp_host, smtp_port?, smtp_username, smtp_secret, from_address, from_name?, daily_limit?}, ...]}`. Verification is **PACED, not parallel** (§4.1, M3-P3-OD-7: strictly serial across the whole batch — `bulk_add_verify_interval_ms` between rows — never per-`smtp_host` in V1): "20 simultaneous auth attempts to one provider looks like credential stuffing." A batch over `bulk_add_max_rows` (M3-P3-OD-8/19) is rejected WHOLE with `422 unprocessable` (`batch_too_large`) BEFORE any row is processed — never partially processed then cut off. Otherwise returns `200` with `{request_id, results: [{row, status: "created"\|"rejected", account_id?, verification?, code?, smtp_response?, details?}, ...]}` — `row` is the 1-based input index. **No transaction spans the batch**: an earlier row's rejection (validation, duplicate, cap) never rolls back a later row's create, and the account cap (§5) is evaluated per row as the batch proceeds, so a batch that crosses the cap mid-way adds rows up to it and rejects the rest with `account_cap_reached`. A row that is created but fails verification is `status: "created"`, `verification: "failed"` — §2.5's same two-orthogonal-facts rule the single-create route uses |
+| DELETE | `/v1/send-byo/accounts/{id}` | M3-Phase 3 | **soft delete** — scoped to `?user_id=<uuid>`, returns `204`. Stamps `deleted_at`/`deleted_by`/`purge_after` (the last computed from the live `account_retention_window_sec`, AT DELETE TIME — a later config change never retroactively moves an existing account's purge date); the row is RETAINED through the window, never removed immediately. Idempotent: a second delete on an already-deleted (or nonexistent) id returns the SAME `404 not_found` a genuinely nonexistent id would — no disclosure of which case it was. A deleted account is IMMEDIATELY unusable through every other verb on this surface (same `404`) and is excluded from dispatch selection (§6.2's consolidated eligibility predicate). The operator's `DELETE /v1/admin/accounts/{id}` remains a **hard** delete on a separate surface (§1.2's two-verbs-two-surfaces split) |

-| **Brain horizontal scaling** | More than one active dispatching Brain. | **Locked out on purpose, not deferred lightly.** The singleton (a session-level Postgres advisory lock) is a CLAUDE.md Rule 7 invariant: "Never add a second dispatch path or distributed dispatch." Exceeding one Brain's throughput is a redesign requiring an ADR and a ruling, not a scaling knob. See [`capacity-planning.md`](./capacity-planning.md) — at realistic V1 volumes account daily limits bind long before the Brain does. |
+| **Control horizontal scaling** | More than one active dispatching Control. | **Locked out on purpose, not deferred lightly.** The singleton (a session-level Postgres advisory lock) is a CLAUDE.md Rule 7 invariant: "Never add a second dispatch path or distributed dispatch." Exceeding one Control's throughput is a redesign requiring an ADR and a ruling, not a scaling knob. See [`capacity-planning.md`](./capacity-planning.md) — at realistic V1 volumes account daily limits bind long before the Control does. |
-| **`/v1/admin/boxes` CRUD** | Registering, listing, and decommissioning boxes over the admin API. | There is **no box route on the admin surface at all** today (verified: the served route set is accounts, pools, config, health). A box is provisioned by seeding a `byosmtp.boxes` row with a bcrypt token hash — `tools/provision-box` mints the pair — and decommissioned by clearing `token_hash`, which refuses it on next connect regardless of a still-valid cert. That works and is documented in [`install-and-deploy.md`](./install-and-deploy.md), but it is a DB operation where every other operator task is an API call. Note the security shape any implementation must preserve: the API may only ever return the token **once, at mint time** (the hash is what is stored), exactly like `smtp_secret`'s write-only posture. |
-| **Server-side bulk credential re-encryption** | Rotating the master key without re-entering every SMTP password by hand. | This is *why* master-key rotation is manual re-entry today, and it is a consequence of a load-bearing security property rather than an oversight: `adminapi` holds an **Encrypt-only** primitive with no `Decrypt` method, and the sole `Decrypt` capability is wired only into the send path (CLAUDE.md Rule 6). A bulk re-encrypt needs a Brain-side path that can decrypt-under-old and encrypt-under-new — i.e. a **second** decrypt call site, in the admin surface. That is exactly what Rule 6 forbids adding casually, so building it requires a ruling on where such a path may live and how it is audited. Procedure as it stands: [`disaster-recovery.md`](./disaster-recovery.md) §3. |
-| **Multi-key credential keyring** | A Brain that resolves more than one `credential_key_id` at a time. | A Brain resolves exactly one label. That constraint is what forces master-key rotation to be freeze-first-then-cut-over (there is no window where rows under two labels are both sendable). A keyring would allow a rolling rotation with no send freeze, and would pair naturally with the item above. |

-| **Per-tenant data isolation beyond RLS** | Anything stronger than `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` on `byosmtp.accounts`. | RLS with a non-login, non-superuser schema owner is the V1 boundary and it genuinely enforces. Stronger isolation (separate schemas or databases per tenant) is a deployment-topology decision. |
-| **A one-call tenant-erasure path** | Making `DELETE FROM public.users` (or an admin endpoint) erase a tenant's byosmtp-module footprint in one operation. | Erasure works today but is a **three-step sequence in this order: accounts → pools → user**. A one-statement user delete is refused by `pools_user_fk`, which declares no referential action — verified by query on real Postgres against a tenant with job history, not assumed. Each step now succeeds (the account step was wedged until `sender_0024`; see ADR-0012). Making the user delete cascade `byosmtp.pools` is a **tenant data-lifecycle ruling**, not a bug fix: it decides whether deleting a platform user may silently destroy byosmtp-module configuration and audit history. Note the audit asymmetry it would inherit — deleting an **account or box** keeps the `job_events` rows with the FK nulled (`SET NULL` + `sender_0024`'s carve-out), whereas deleting the **user** removes them outright (`job_events_user_fk` is `ON DELETE CASCADE`). Both are intended, but a one-call path must document which one the caller gets. |

-| **Zero the box's in-flight credential on shutdown and on an uncaught exception** | The box's SIGTERM/SIGINT handler stops the stream and exits without zeroing the credential the current send holds, and no `uncaughtException`/`unhandledRejection` handler is registered at all. The three send-path exits (accept, SMTP error, thrown exception) *are* covered by a `finally` and are tested. | A memory image captured at that instant — core dump, container checkpoint, `/proc/<pid>/mem` — may hold one in-flight plaintext. The fix is small (give `stop()` a reference to the live credential; add the two process handlers) but it changes the shutdown path of the service that holds credentials, and it needs its own behavioral test per Rule 3. Consequence documented at [`security-posture.md`](./security-posture.md) §3.12, which is what stops an operator believing `systemctl stop` is a scrub. |
-| **Revoke-on-live-stream: terminate or periodically re-authorize a connected box** | The token/status check runs **only** in the register handshake. Job pushes are served from an in-memory box map with no re-read of `byosmtp.boxes`, and the heartbeat path returns a `stale` box to `active` without re-checking the token. | So clearing `token_hash` refuses the next connect but does not disconnect a box that is already streaming — an attacker who keeps the (outbound, box-initiated) stream open keeps receiving one plaintext credential per job. Closing it means either a re-authorization read on the push path (a DB read per push, on the hottest path in the system) or a Brain-side stream-kill triggered by a config/DB signal — both real design decisions, not polish. The interim answer is procedural and now documented: isolate the host **first**, revoke second ([`disaster-recovery.md`](./disaster-recovery.md) §4a, [`security-posture.md`](./security-posture.md) §3.1). |

-| **Reject private-range `smtp_host` at write time, or gate the self-signed affordance behind an explicit dev flag** | The box disables TLS certificate verification for loopback/RFC-1918/link-local SMTP hosts — a test affordance so the harness can reach the local sink — while the Brain-side validator accepts any bare IP literal. | The two together mean a real account can be pointed at a private address and will AUTH over an unverified connection. -| **Restrict the alert webhook's destination** | Reject loopback, RFC-1918, and link-local (`169.254.0.0/16`, i.e. cloud metadata) destinations for `alert_webhook_url`, or take an allowlist. | Validation today is a scheme-prefix check only, so the Brain will POST from inside the trust boundary to any reachable address — a blind SSRF available to a Domain B holder. Bounded (only an already-privileged principal can set it; the response is never returned or logged) but real. A blocklist has to be a config decision rather than a hardcoded constant, per Rule 1. [`security-posture.md`](./security-posture.md) §3.14. |
-| **An append-only `config_events` audit table** | A durable, tamper-resistant row per config write, with the key, the before value, the after value, and the request id. | Config writes are recorded **only** as a Brain process-log line today — no DB row, no before/after. So "when was `debug_log_retention_days` widened?" (§3.2 makes that a privacy question) is answerable only from shipped logs, for as long as their retention holds. New table + new write path on every `PUT /v1/admin/config`. [`security-posture.md`](./security-posture.md) §3.6. |
-| **Per-send attestation** | Something that lets the Brain distinguish a truthful box report from a fabricated one. | The outcome guards check the reporting box against `assigned_box_id` and the `attempt_token` against the current attempt, which stops replay across attempts and boxes — but a compromised box can still report any outcome for the job it legitimately holds: `accepted` for mail never sent, or fabricated `auth_failure`s that quarantine healthy accounts. §3.9's absent delivery feedback means neither is detectable here. This is a protocol-level design problem (what could a box sign that the Brain cannot already forge on its behalf?), not an implementation gap. [`security-posture.md`](./security-posture.md) §3.15. |
-| **A credential-leak scan that runs against a production log stream** | An operator-runnable check that a real deployment's shipped logs contain no credential. | The blocking `no_secret_leak` CI gate reads `.env` and compares the **dev box token and its hash** against *dev compose* logs; the SMTP-credential canary scan lives in the send-path harness and needs the whole dev stack. +| **A register rejection short-circuits the documented ~30-attempt retry budget.** | `services/worker/src/stream.js` calls `this.stop()` on `accepted:false`, which sets `stopped = true`, so `connectOnce` returns immediately at the top of its next iteration. **Measured:** exit after attempt 1, ~1s, not ~30 attempts over ~30s. | The budget is real but covers **dial/TLS failures only**; a rejection is treated as terminal on purpose (an unauthorized worker hammering the Control is worse than a worker that exits for its supervisor to restart). What is wrong is the *documentation* of the budget's scope, plus the interaction with the item above. Changing the retry behavior is behavior; the doc side is being corrected. |
+| **Three inert variables in `.env.example`: `SEND_BYO_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL`, `PLATFORM_SERVICE_TOKEN`, `PLATFORM_ADMIN_KEY_HASH`.** | No code reads any of the three. The webhook destination comes only from the `alert_webhook_url` config row; the live auth variables are `PLATFORM_TOKEN_HASHES` and `ADMIN_API_KEY_HASHES`, both comma-separated **bcrypt** lists — not a plaintext token, not a SHA-256. | Setting the env var and expecting alerts is a silent no-op — a config-not-code violation in an *example file*, not in the running system. Setting any of them expecting an effect is a silent no-op, and for the two auth ones the surface fails **closed** — a Domain A call returns `401` with no hint that the variable you set is not the one being read. Removing the lines is trivial but touches the example every install copies; all three are now labelled inert in `.env.example` itself, and noted in [`monitoring.md`](./monitoring.md) §3 and [`install-and-deploy.md`](./install-and-deploy.md) Step 6, so nobody is misled meanwhile. |

-- **A second box.** Multi-box routing, box death, and reclaim all need one to mean anything. `scripts/dev.sh certs` provisions it and `scripts/dev.sh reset` seeds it; start it with **`scripts/dev.sh up2`**. -  - **Do not use `docker compose up --scale box=2`.** Box identity is the authorization subject: scaled replicas share one `BOX_ID`/`BOX_TOKEN`, and the Brain closes the previous connection whenever an id re-registers (the correct reconnect rule). Two same-id replicas evict each other in a permanent register/disconnect loop, `byosmtp.boxes` still shows one row, and no work is distributed. The two boxes intentionally **share** the dev mTLS cert — the cert is transport, the token is the authority.
+- **A second worker.** Multi-worker routing, worker death, and reclaim all need one to mean anything. `scripts/dev.sh certs` provisions it and `scripts/dev.sh reset` seeds it; start it with **`scripts/dev.sh up2`**. +  - **Do not use `docker compose up --scale worker=2`.** Worker identity is the authorization subject: scaled replicas share one `WORKER_ID`/`WORKER_TOKEN`, and the Control closes the previous connection whenever an id re-registers (the correct reconnect rule). Two same-id replicas evict each other in a permanent register/disconnect loop, `send_byo.boxes` still shows one row, and no work is distributed. The two workers intentionally **share** the dev mTLS cert — the cert is transport, the token is the authority.
-- **A reset drops the box rows, and `--wait` will lie to you about it.** `reset` is `down -v`, which destroys the volume holding `byosmtp.boxes` — so a box has nothing to authorize against, is refused with `unauthenticated`, burns its retry budget and **exits 1**. `up --wait` reports it *healthy* seconds before it dies, so a scripted run sees a green light on a dead box. `reset` now re-seeds the box rows itself (postgres → migrate → seed → the rest); if you drive compose by hand, run `scripts/dev.sh seed` after migrations and before the box. Always confirm with `docker compose ps -a` (**`-a`** — a plain `ps` hides an exited container).
+- **A reset drops the worker rows, and `--wait` will lie to you about it.** `reset` is `down -v`, which destroys the volume holding `send_byo.boxes` — so a worker has nothing to authorize against, is refused with `unauthenticated`, burns its retry budget and **exits 1**. `up --wait` reports it *healthy* seconds before it dies, so a scripted run sees a green light on a dead worker. `reset` now re-seeds the worker rows itself (postgres → migrate → seed → the rest); if you drive compose by hand, run `scripts/dev.sh seed` after migrations and before the worker. Always confirm with `docker compose ps -a` (**`-a`** — a plain `ps` hides an exited container).
-  - So: a bare `docker compose up -d --force-recreate --wait brain` to pick up a rebuilt Brain will take postgres with it if the previous `up` came from `dev.sh`. Rebuild through `dev.sh`, or add `--no-deps`, and re-check your fixtures (`SELECT count(*) FROM byosmtp.jobs`) before trusting a result. Anything you must keep across a restart belongs in a re-runnable seed step, not in the database only.
+  - So: a bare `docker compose up -d --force-recreate --wait control` to pick up a rebuilt Control will take postgres with it if the previous `up` came from `dev.sh`. +-- send_byo_0000_bootstrap.up.sql — Phase 0 pre-feature bootstrap (ADR-0002).
+-- Numbered 0000 (pre-feature groundwork) so the LOCKED feature chain stays exactly
+-- send_byo_0001..send_byo_0020 as every Phase 1–9 spec and the Phase 9 §4 config reference assume.
+-- Creates the EMPTY send_byo schema owned by a non-login/non-superuser owner (OD-13/ADR-0004),
+-- the login app role, the migration tracking table, and the enumerated grants. It creates
+-- NO feature tables, enums, or config — those are Phase 1+ (the feature chain begins at
+-- send_byo_0001_create_schema). Runs as an admin/owner-capable role (OD-1). Role passwords are
+-- NEVER in migration SQL.
+
+-- 1) Roles. Idempotent guards so this is safe under managed/out-of-band role provisioning.
+DO $$
+BEGIN
+    -- send_byo_owner: OWNS the schema so FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY actually enforces against
+    -- the app role. NOLOGIN, NOSUPERUSER, NOCREATEROLE, NOCREATEDB.
+    IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'send_byo_owner') THEN
+        CREATE ROLE send_byo_owner NOLOGIN NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEROLE NOCREATEDB;
+    END IF;
+    -- send_byo_app: the LOGIN app role the Control connects as at runtime. Password is set
+    -- OUT-OF-BAND (ALTER ROLE ... PASSWORD) — never here.
+    IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'send_byo_app') THEN
+        CREATE ROLE send_byo_app LOGIN NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEROLE NOCREATEDB;
+    END IF;
+END $$;
+
+-- 2) Schema, owned by send_byo_owner; deny PUBLIC (defense in depth).
+CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS send_byo AUTHORIZATION send_byo_owner;
+REVOKE ALL ON SCHEMA send_byo FROM PUBLIC;
+GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA send_byo TO send_byo_app;
+
+-- 3) Migration tracking table — owned by send_byo_owner, one row per migration (self-tracked).
+CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS send_byo.schema_migrations (
+    version    TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
+    applied_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
+);
+ALTER TABLE send_byo.schema_migrations OWNER TO send_byo_owner;
+-- The runner and migrations (admin role) read/write this; send_byo_app may read it.
+GRANT SELECT ON send_byo.schema_migrations TO send_byo_app;
+
+-- 4) Default privileges: objects FUTURE migrations create AS send_byo_owner are granted to
+--    send_byo_app automatically. Append-only REVOKEs + platform-table SELECTs are issued
+--    by their own Phase-1 migrations (e.g. send_byo_0012 grants/RLS), not here.
+ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE send_byo_owner IN SCHEMA send_byo
+    GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON TABLES TO send_byo_app;
+ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE send_byo_owner IN SCHEMA send_byo
+    GRANT USAGE, SELECT ON SEQUENCES TO send_byo_app;
+
+-- 5) The ONLY two operations permitted on platform-owned tables: read-only SELECT.
+--    Preflight (run before this) guarantees the tables exist.
+GRANT SELECT ON public.users     TO send_byo_app;
+GRANT SELECT ON public.job_items TO send_byo_app;
+
+-- 6) Self-record (locked convention — the runner does NOT write this row; the file does).
+INSERT INTO send_byo.schema_migrations (version) VALUES ('0000');
+-- send_byo_0001_create_schema.down.sql — reverse of the feature-chain start.
+-- bootstrap (send_byo_0000) and are torn down only by send_byo_0000's own down. Reversing 0001
-DELETE FROM byosmtp.schema_migrations WHERE version = '0001';
+DELETE FROM send_byo.schema_migrations WHERE version = '0001';
+-- send_byo_0001_create_schema.up.sql — Phase 1 feature chain start (data model).
+-- The `sender` schema, its non-login owner `send_byo_owner`, the login app role `send_byo_app`,
+-- and `send_byo.schema_migrations` were ALL created by the Phase 0 pre-feature bootstrap
+-- (send_byo_0000, ADR-0002). This migration is therefore an IDEMPOTENT confirmation of that
+-- ground — it re-asserts schema existence + PUBLIC lockout without dropping anything the
+-- bootstrap owns. It records version 0001 so the locked feature chain (send_byo_0001..0020, per
+-- every Phase 1–9 spec + Phase 9 §4) begins exactly here, unshifted.
+--
+-- Runs as the admin/owner-capable migration role (OD-1). Idempotent: safe to re-run.
+
+-- Confirm the schema exists and is denied to PUBLIC (defense in depth). The bootstrap already
+-- did `CREATE SCHEMA send_byo AUTHORIZATION send_byo_owner`; this is a no-op re-assertion on the
+-- established ground, never a re-create that would change ownership.
+CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS send_byo AUTHORIZATION send_byo_owner;
+REVOKE ALL ON SCHEMA send_byo FROM PUBLIC;
+
+-- send_byo.schema_migrations already exists (bootstrap). Re-assert idempotently so this file is
+-- self-contained if ever applied against a hand-built schema, without disturbing 0000's row.
+CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS send_byo.schema_migrations (
+    version    TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
+    applied_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
+);
+
+-- Self-record (locked convention — the runner does NOT write this row; the file does).
+INSERT INTO send_byo.schema_migrations (version) VALUES ('0001');
+-- send_byo_0002_create_role.down.sql — reverse of the role-confirmation migration.
+-- 0002 only re-asserted the bootstrap's role + default privileges; it created nothing new.
+-- The role send_byo_app and the base default-privilege grants are owned by the Phase 0
+-- bootstrap (send_byo_0000) and are reversed only by its down. So this DOWN un-records 0002
+-- only — it must NOT drop the role (dropping it would break the still-applied bootstrap and
+-- fail anyway if the role owns/holds objects).
+DELETE FROM send_byo.schema_migrations WHERE version = '0002';
+-- send_byo_0002_create_role.up.sql — Phase 1: confirm the app role + default privileges.
+-- The `send_byo_app` LOGIN role and the `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE send_byo_owner ...
+-- GRANT ... TO send_byo_app` were established by the Phase 0 bootstrap (send_byo_0000). This
+-- migration idempotently re-asserts them so the feature chain is self-contained, WITHOUT
+-- recreating the role or changing ownership. Role password is NEVER set in migration SQL
+-- (out-of-band via ALTER ROLE / the runner's set-app-password step, OD-1).
+
+-- Confirm the login role exists (bootstrap created it; guard makes this safe to re-run).
+DO $$
+BEGIN
+    IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'send_byo_app') THEN
+        CREATE ROLE send_byo_app LOGIN NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEROLE NOCREATEDB;
+    END IF;
+END $$;
+
+-- USAGE on the schema + default privileges on FUTURE tables/sequences that send_byo_owner
+-- creates. Re-asserting is idempotent (GRANT is additive; ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES is
+-- last-writer). This keeps every feature table (0004+) usable by send_byo_app without a
+-- per-table grant, matching the bootstrap posture. The append-only REVOKEs that narrow
+-- job_events/send_logs land in their own creating migrations (0008/0009), per ADR-0002.
+GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA send_byo TO send_byo_app;
+ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE send_byo_owner IN SCHEMA send_byo
+    GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON TABLES TO send_byo_app;
+ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE send_byo_owner IN SCHEMA send_byo
+    GRANT USAGE, SELECT ON SEQUENCES TO send_byo_app;
+
+-- Self-record.
+INSERT INTO send_byo.schema_migrations (version) VALUES ('0002');

+-- send_byo_0012_grants_and_rls.up.sql — Phase 1: table-level DML grants to send_byo_app + RLS.
+--
+-- Reconciliation note (ground = Phase 0 send_byo_0000): the bootstrap's `ALTER DEFAULT
+-- PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE send_byo_owner ... GRANT ... TO send_byo_app` keys on the *creator* of an
+-- object. Phase 1 feature tables are created by the admin migration role and then
+-- `ALTER ... OWNER TO send_byo_owner`, so default privileges do NOT fire — send_byo_app receives
+-- NO DML on the feature tables until the EXPLICIT grants below. This is stronger for the
+-- append-only invariant: job_events is born with zero send_byo_app DML and receives only
+-- INSERT+SELECT here (never UPDATE/DELETE); send_logs receives INSERT+SELECT+DELETE (never
+-- UPDATE). The 0008/0009 REVOKEs remain as defense-in-depth / intent, even though they are
+-- no-ops against a table that was never granted UPDATE/DELETE.
+--
+-- The two read-only platform-table grants (public.users, public.job_items) are owned by the
+-- bootstrap (send_byo_0000) and are deliberately NOT re-issued or revoked here — so rolling back
+-- 0012 never disturbs a grant the still-applied bootstrap owns.
+
+-- === Table DML grants (mutable tables: full DML) ========================================
+GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON send_byo.pools    TO send_byo_app;
+GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON send_byo.accounts TO send_byo_app;
+GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON send_byo.boxes    TO send_byo_app;
+GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON send_byo.jobs     TO send_byo_app;
+GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON send_byo.config   TO send_byo_app;
+
+-- Append-only tables: exactly the privileges each allows (matches 0008/0009 REVOKE posture).
+GRANT SELECT, INSERT         ON send_byo.job_events TO send_byo_app;  -- no UPDATE, no DELETE
+GRANT SELECT, INSERT, DELETE ON send_byo.send_logs TO send_byo_app;  -- no UPDATE (retention needs DELETE)
+
+-- Sequences (job_events.seq IDENTITY). gen_random_uuid() PKs need none, but grant for safety.
+GRANT USAGE, SELECT ON ALL SEQUENCES IN SCHEMA send_byo TO send_byo_app;
+
+-- === Row-Level Security =================================================================
+-- ENABLE RLS on all sender.* tables; FORCE on send_byo.accounts (crown jewel). send_byo_app
+-- gets a permissive USING(true)/WITH CHECK(true) policy (it is the trusted cross-tenant
+-- dispatcher — tenant scoping is a module-query responsibility, not RLS). Every OTHER role
+-- gets no policy => default-deny (backstops a future misgrant). FORCE binds even the table
+-- owner (send_byo_owner) to the policy; a superuser still bypasses (credential secrecy rests on
+-- encryption, §9).
+ALTER TABLE send_byo.pools       ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
+ALTER TABLE send_byo.accounts    ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
+ALTER TABLE send_byo.accounts    FORCE  ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
+ALTER TABLE send_byo.boxes       ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
+ALTER TABLE send_byo.jobs        ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
+ALTER TABLE send_byo.config      ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
+ALTER TABLE send_byo.job_events  ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
+ALTER TABLE send_byo.send_logs   ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

+// TestClassify_Table drives the §1.1 mapping table with real SMTP response strings (the exact
+// forms the T1 sink returns in Chunk 6's full-pipe suite) and asserts the resulting error_class.
+// classifyReport is pure, so this is a faithful, non-vacuous oracle: each case's class is driven
+// by the real reply code + enhanced code + text, first-match-wins, NOT by an injected class.
+func TestClassify_Table(t *testing.T) {
+	cases := []struct {
+		name string
+		rep  workerproto.Report
+		want string
+	}{
+		// Row 1 — success has no class.
+		{"accepted_no_class", workerproto.Report{Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeAccepted}, ""},
+
+		// Row 1-of-2 — a reported bounce is always permanent (worker decided at RCPT TO).
+		{"reported_bounce", workerproto.Report{Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeBounced, SMTPResponse: "550 5.1.1 No such user"}, classBouncePermanent},
+
+		// Row 2 — 550 WITH recipient-invalid signal → bounce_permanent (enhanced code path).
+		{"550_enh_511", workerproto.Report{Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeError, SMTPResponse: "550 5.1.1 No such user here"}, classBouncePermanent},
+		// Row 2 — 550 WITH recipient-invalid signal → bounce_permanent (TEXT path, no enhanced code).
+		{"550_text_unknown", workerproto.Report{Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeError, SMTPResponse: "550 mailbox unavailable"}, classBouncePermanent},
+		{"551_text", workerproto.Report{Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeError, SMTPResponse: "551 User unknown; not local"}, classBouncePermanent},
+
+		// Row 7 (NEGATIVE control for row 2) — a bare policy 550 with NO recipient signal must NOT
+		// bounce; conservative → unknown (recipient may be valid, re-route via another account).
+		{"550_policy_57x_is_unknown", workerproto.Report{Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeError, SMTPResponse: "550 5.7.1 Message blocked by policy"}, classUnknown},
+		{"550_no_signal_is_unknown", workerproto.Report{Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeError, SMTPResponse: "550 Rejected"}, classUnknown},
+
+		// Row 3 — auth_failure via reply code, enhanced code, and worker slugs.
+		{"535_code", workerproto.Report{Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeError, SMTPResponse: "535 5.7.8 Authentication credentials invalid"}, classAuthFailure},
+		{"534_code", workerproto.Report{Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeError, SMTPResponse: "534 5.7.9 Please use a different auth mechanism"}, classAuthFailure},
+		{"530_code", workerproto.Report{Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeError, SMTPResponse: "530 5.7.0 Authentication required"}, classAuthFailure},
+		{"538_encryption_required", workerproto.Report{Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeError, SMTPResponse: "538 5.7.11 Encryption required for requested auth"}, classAuthFailure},
+		{"auth_failed_slug", workerproto.Report{Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeError, ErrorReason: workerproto.ReasonAuthFailed, SMTPResponse: ""}, classAuthFailure},
+		{"starttls_unavail_slug_is_auth", workerproto.Report{Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeError, ErrorReason: workerproto.ReasonStartTLSUnavail, SMTPResponse: ""}, classAuthFailure},
+
+		// Row 4 — throttle: 4xx WITH a rate/volume signal (text keyword OR provider 4.2.1).
+		{"421_too_many", workerproto.Report{Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeError, SMTPResponse: "421 4.7.0 Too many messages, rate limited"}, classThrottle},
+		{"450_rate", workerproto.Report{Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeError, SMTPResponse: "450 4.2.1 The user has exceeded their sending limit"}, classThrottle},
+		{"452_quota", workerproto.Report{Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeError, SMTPResponse: "452 Insufficient system storage, quota exceeded"}, classThrottle},
+
+		// Row 5 (NEGATIVE control for row 4) — a 4xx with NO rate signal is transport_4xx, NOT
+		// throttle: it must not pause the account. This is the throttle/transient teeth.
+		{"451_temp_local", workerproto.Report{Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeError, SMTPResponse: "451 4.3.0 Temporary local error, try again"}, classTransport4xx},
+		{"450_greylist", workerproto.Report{Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeError, SMTPResponse: "450 4.2.0 Greylisted, please retry"}, classTransport4xx},
+		{"data_4xx_slug", workerproto.Report{Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeError, ErrorReason: workerproto.ReasonDataRejected4xx, SMTPResponse: ""}, classTransport4xx},
+
+		// Row 6 — timeout: connectivity/no-response/deadline slugs (policy == transport_4xx, class
+		// distinct). Includes worker-internal transport slugs not in the canonical §2.4 set.
+		{"connect_refused", workerproto.Report{Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeError, ErrorReason: workerproto.ReasonConnectRefused, SMTPResponse: ""}, classTimeout},
+		{"timeout_slug", workerproto.Report{Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeError, ErrorReason: workerproto.ReasonTimeout, SMTPResponse: ""}, classTimeout},
+		{"lease_expired", workerproto.Report{Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeError, ErrorReason: workerproto.ReasonLeaseExpired, SMTPResponse: ""}, classTimeout},
+		{"connection_closed", workerproto.Report{Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeError, ErrorReason: reasonConnectionClosed, SMTPResponse: ""}, classTimeout},
+		{"starttls_failed_is_timeout", workerproto.Report{Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeError, ErrorReason: reasonStartTLSFailed, SMTPResponse: ""}, classTimeout},
+
+		// Row 7 — unknown: ambiguous permanent-ish 5xx not matched above, and the 5xx slug.
+		{"554_generic", workerproto.Report{Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeError, SMTPResponse: "554 5.7.1 Transaction failed"}, classUnknown},
+		{"552_quota_5xx", workerproto.Report{Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeError, SMTPResponse: "552 5.2.2 Mailbox full"}, classUnknown},
+		{"data_5xx_slug", workerproto.Report{Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeError, ErrorReason: workerproto.ReasonDataRejected5xx, SMTPResponse: ""}, classUnknown},
+
+		// Row 8 — unknown catch-all: unparseable, accepted_without_id, empty.
+		{"garbage", workerproto.Report{Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeError, SMTPResponse: "wat"}, classUnknown},
+		{"accepted_without_id", workerproto.Report{Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeError, ErrorReason: workerproto.ReasonAcceptedWithoutID, SMTPResponse: ""}, classUnknown},
+		{"empty", workerproto.Report{Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeError, SMTPResponse: "", ErrorReason: ""}, classUnknown},
+	}
+	for _, c := range cases {
+		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			got := classifyReport(c.rep)
+			if got != c.want {
+				t.Fatalf("classifyReport(%q / reason=%q) = %q, want %q", c.rep.SMTPResponse, c.rep.ErrorReason, got, c.want)
+			}
+		})
+	}
+}
+
+// TestClassify_CodeDominatesText proves the ordering rule: the reply CODE decides the class; a
+// text keyword only disambiguates WITHIN a code, never overrides it. A 535 (auth) that happens to
+// contain the word "rate" must still classify as auth_failure, NOT throttle — code wins.
+func TestClassify_CodeDominatesText(t *testing.T) {
+	rep := workerproto.Report{Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeError, SMTPResponse: "535 5.7.8 auth failed (too many attempts, rate limited)"}
+	if got := classifyReport(rep); got != classAuthFailure {
+		t.Fatalf("535 with 'rate' text = %q, want auth_failure (code dominates text)", got)
+	}
+	// And a bounce 550 with recipient text is not derailed by an incidental "try again later".
+	rep2 := workerproto.Report{Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeError, SMTPResponse: "550 5.1.1 no such user (try again later won't help)"}
+	if got := classifyReport(rep2); got != classBouncePermanent {
+		t.Fatalf("550 5.1.1 recipient bounce = %q, want bounce_permanent", got)
+	}
+}

+// Phase 7 review gate R3 — the one-in-flight marker vs a REPLAYED report (§2.5 × §1.3/§2.3).
+//
+// Phase 7 turned `report` from a once-per-job frame into a REPEATABLE one: the worker replays every
+// unacked outcome on each heartbeat tick and on each reconnect. dispatchFrame used to clear the worker's
+// in-flight marker on ANY report, so a replay for an OLD job cleared the marker of the NEW job the worker
+// was actually running — the dispatcher then saw the worker as idle and pushed a SECOND job (with a
+// SECOND decrypted credential) to a worker already mid-SMTP. That breaks one-job-per-worker (§2.5) and, since
+// the worker's #runJob is fire-and-forget, it genuinely runs two sessions holding two credentials.
+//
+// This exercises the REAL StreamServer state machine (real workerConn, real dispatchFrame, real PushJob,
+// real AnyConnectedWorker) over a real in-process socket pair. No DB is needed: the marker lives entirely
+// in memory and the frames under test (report) take no DB path when onReport is the identity handler.
+
+import (
+	"encoding/json"
+	"net"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/coldmail-send-byo/control/internal/workerproto"
+)
+
+// newMarkerServer builds a StreamServer with ONE registered worker, bypassing only the TLS listener and
+// the register handshake (both proven by the live-stack mTLS suite): everything the test asserts on —
+// the workers map, workerConn.inFlight, dispatchFrame, PushJob, AnyConnectedWorker — is the production code.
+func newMarkerServer(t *testing.T, workerID string, onReport ReportHandler) (*StreamServer, net.Conn) {
+	t.Helper()
+	server, client := net.Pipe()
+	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = server.Close(); _ = client.Close() })
+	// Drain whatever the server writes so a frame write never blocks on the pipe.
+	go func() {
+		buf := make([]byte, 4096)
+		for {
+			if _, err := client.Read(buf); err != nil {
+				return
+			}
+		}
+	}()
+	s := &StreamServer{
+		onReport: onReport,
+		workers:    make(map[string]*workerConn),
+		closed:   make(chan struct{}),
+	}
+	s.workers[workerID] = &workerConn{conn: server, enc: json.NewEncoder(server), workerID: workerID}
+	return s, server
+}
+
+func frame(t *testing.T, v any) []byte {
+	t.Helper()
+	b, err := json.Marshal(v)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("marshal frame: %v", err)
+	}
+	return b
+}
+
+// TestInFlightMarker_ReplayedReportDoesNotFreeALiveJob is the regression test for R3's HIGH finding.
+//
+// Sequence, exactly as production produces it: job-OLD's outcome went unacked (DB outage) and is
+// buffered on the worker; the outage ends; the Control pushes job-NEW to that same worker; mid-SMTP the worker's
+// heartbeat tick replays job-OLD's report. Asserts the replay does NOT make the worker push-eligible.
+//
+// Paired positive control: the report for the job the worker is ACTUALLY holding DOES clear the marker, so
+// the guard cannot pass by simply never clearing (which would wedge every worker after its first job).
+func TestInFlightMarker_ReplayedReportDoesNotFreeALiveJob(t *testing.T) {
+	const workerID = "worker-marker"
+	var reported []string
+	s, _ := newMarkerServer(t, workerID, func(_ string, rep workerproto.Report) bool {
+		reported = append(reported, rep.JobID)
+		return true // persisted (the ack path is proven elsewhere; irrelevant to the marker)
+	})
+
+	// The worker is holding job-NEW (the real push path sets the marker).
+	if err := s.PushJob(workerproto.PushJob{Type: workerproto.TypePushJob, RequestID: "req-new", JobID: "job-NEW"}, workerID); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("push job-NEW: %v", err)
+	}
+	if got := s.AnyConnectedWorker(); got != "" {
+		t.Fatalf("AnyConnectedWorker=%q while the worker holds job-NEW, want \"\" (one-in-flight, §2.5)", got)
+	}
+
+	// *** THE REPLAY ***: a buffered outcome for a DIFFERENT, older job arrives on the live stream.
+	s.dispatchFrame(workerID, frame(t, workerproto.Report{
+		Type: workerproto.TypeReport, RequestID: "req-old", JobID: "job-OLD", Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeAccepted,
+		ProviderMessageID: "pmid-old", SMTPResponse: "250 2.0.0 OK",
+	}))
+
+	// The replay must still reach the outcome handler (it is a real outcome that may need persisting —
+	// dropping it would lose it, and the worker would replay forever).
+	if len(reported) != 1 || reported[0] != "job-OLD" {
+		t.Fatalf("replayed report reached the handler as %v, want [job-OLD] — the marker guard must not swallow the outcome", reported)
+	}
+	// ...but it must NOT have freed the live job's marker.
+	s.mu.Lock()
+	held := s.workers[workerID].inFlight
+	s.mu.Unlock()
+	if held != "job-NEW" {
+		t.Fatalf("in-flight marker is %q after a replayed report for job-OLD, want job-NEW — a stale replay freed a LIVE job's slot", held)
+	}
+	if got := s.AnyConnectedWorker(); got != "" {
+		t.Fatalf("AnyConnectedWorker=%q after a replayed report for an old job — the dispatcher now believes a worker mid-SMTP is idle", got)
+	}
+	// The concrete harm, asserted directly: a SECOND push (a second plaintext credential) would succeed.
+	if err := s.PushJob(workerproto.PushJob{Type: workerproto.TypePushJob, RequestID: "req-2nd", JobID: "job-SECOND"}, workerID); err == nil {
+		t.Fatal("PushJob ACCEPTED a second concurrent job after a replayed report — two jobs and TWO plaintext credentials on one worker at once (§2.5 broken)")
+	}
+
+	// ---- POSITIVE CONTROL: the report for the job actually held DOES clear the marker. ----
+	s.dispatchFrame(workerID, frame(t, workerproto.Report{
+		Type: workerproto.TypeReport, RequestID: "req-new", JobID: "job-NEW", Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeAccepted,
+		ProviderMessageID: "pmid-new", SMTPResponse: "250 2.0.0 OK",
+	}))
+	s.mu.Lock()
+	held = s.workers[workerID].inFlight
+	s.mu.Unlock()
+	if held != "" {
+		t.Fatalf("in-flight marker is %q after the OWNING job's report, want \"\" — the worker would never be pushed to again", held)
+	}
+	if got := s.AnyConnectedWorker(); got != workerID {
+		t.Fatalf("AnyConnectedWorker=%q after the owning report, want %q — the worker must become eligible again", got, workerID)
+	}
+	if err := s.PushJob(workerproto.PushJob{Type: workerproto.TypePushJob, RequestID: "req-3rd", JobID: "job-THIRD"}, workerID); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("PushJob refused the next job after a clean completion: %v", err)
+	}
+}
+
+// TestInFlightMarker_ReplayOnAnIdleWorkerIsHarmless covers the other replay shape: the worker finished its
+// job, was acked-less, and replays while IDLE. The marker is already "" and must stay "" — the worker
+// remains eligible (a replay must not wedge a healthy idle worker out of the dispatch pool).
+func TestInFlightMarker_ReplayOnAnIdleWorkerIsHarmless(t *testing.T) {
+	const workerID = "worker-idle"
+	s, _ := newMarkerServer(t, workerID, func(_ string, _ workerproto.Report) bool { return true })
+
+	if got := s.AnyConnectedWorker(); got != workerID {
+		t.Fatalf("precondition: AnyConnectedWorker=%q, want %q (an idle registered worker is eligible)", got, workerID)
+	}
+	s.dispatchFrame(workerID, frame(t, workerproto.Report{
+		Type: workerproto.TypeReport, RequestID: "req-old", JobID: "job-OLD", Outcome: workerproto.OutcomeAccepted,
+		ProviderMessageID: "pmid-old", SMTPResponse: "250 2.0.0 OK",
+	}))
+	s.mu.Lock()
+	held := s.workers[workerID].inFlight
+	s.mu.Unlock()
+	if held != "" {
+		t.Fatalf("in-flight marker became %q from a replay on an IDLE worker — the worker is now permanently ineligible", held)
+	}
+	if got := s.AnyConnectedWorker(); got != workerID {
+		t.Fatalf("AnyConnectedWorker=%q after an idle-worker replay, want %q", got, workerID)
+	}
